sys_remote_update_set.description: The two global-scope business rules that do not travel with the scoped application: ClaimEase - Enforce Receipt On Submitted, and ClaimEase - Restore Claim On Receipt.
sys_remote_update_set.name: ClaimEase - global business rules (receipt enforcement)

<record_update table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <abort_action>false</abort_action> <access>package_private</access> <action_delete>false</action_delete> <action_insert>true</action_insert> <action_query>false</action_query> <action_update>false</action_update> <active>true</active> <add_message>false</add_message> <advanced>true</advanced> <change_fields>false</change_fields> <client_callable>false</client_callable> <collection>x_2180676_claime_0_claim</collection> <condition/> <description>Enforces the receipt requirement on the insert-as-submitted path, which Validate Claim (order 200) deliberately skips. Returns a receiptless claim to draft and cancels any approvals already requested.</description> <execute_function>false</execute_function> <filter_condition table="x_2180676_claime_0_claim">approval_statusINsubmitted,pending_manager,pending_finance<item goto="false" or="false" field="approval_status" endquery="false" value="submitted,pending_manager,pending_finance" operator="IN" newquery="false"/> </filter_condition> <is_rest>false</is_rest> <message/> <name>ClaimEase - Enforce Receipt On Submitted</name> <order>2000</order> <priority>100</priority> <rest_method/> <rest_method_text/> <rest_service/> <rest_service_text/> <rest_variables/> <role_conditions/> <script><![CDATA[/** * ClaimEase - Enforce Receipt On Submitted Insert (async, after insert, order 2000) * * PURPOSE * Closes the one path on which the receipt requirement was not enforced. * * "Validate Claim" (order 200) asks ClaimEaseValidator for the receipt check * only when `!isInsert && enteringSubmitted`, because an attachment cannot * exist before the record does. That is correct for the draft -> submitted * transition, but it leaves the INSERT-as-submitted path unchecked, and that * is the path the record producer uses: it sets approval_status = 'submitted' * in the insert itself and passes checkReceipt: false, relying on the catalog * item's `mandatory_attachment` flag. * * `mandatory_attachment` is a client-side catalog control. It is enforced by * the portal widget, not by the save, so it is absent for a direct POST to * submit_producer, for the Table API, for server scripts and for flows. A * claim could therefore be submitted, routed and fully approved with no * receipt at all (reproduced on CLM0001069). * * WHY ASYNC RATHER THAN A SYNCHRONOUS AFTER-INSERT RULE * On the record producer path the attachment is copied onto the claim AFTER * the row is inserted. A synchronous after-insert rule can therefore run * before the receipt has landed and would wrongly reject legitimate portal * submissions. An async rule runs once the transaction has committed, by * which time the attachment is present, so a genuine portal claim with a * receipt is untouched. * * WHAT IT DOES ON A MISS * The claim is returned to `draft` and `flow_started` is cleared, so it is no * longer an eligible claim and the approval flow's own eligibility guard * (claim still `submitted`) stops any run that had already begun. Approval * records the flow may already have requested are cancelled, so no approver * is left holding a decision on a claim that is no longer live. The reason is * recorded on `exception_reason` so the employee can attach the receipt and * submit again. * * It deliberately does NOT touch manager_approval or finance_approval: those * fields are guarded by "Protect Approval Fields", and the claim has not been * decided yet, so there is nothing to undo on them. * * FAIL CLOSED * ClaimEaseValidator.hasAttachment() returns false when it cannot prove an * attachment exists. A claim is therefore returned to draft when the receipt * cannot be confirmed, rather than being left approvable on an unproven one. */ (function executeRule(current, previous) { var config = new x_2180676_claime_0.ClaimEaseConfig()
if (!config.requireReceipt()) { return } // The approval flow moves the claim off `submitted` within seconds of the // insert, and this rule runs after the transaction has committed, so the // status is usually `pending_manager` by now. Check the whole set of live // states rather than `submitted` alone, or the rule silently never fires. var LIVE_STATES = ['submitted', 'pending_manager', 'pending_finance'] var statusNow = '' + (current.getValue('approval_status') || '') gs.info('[ClaimEase] Receipt check running for claim ' + current.getValue('number') + ' (status ' + statusNow + ').') if (LIVE_STATES.indexOf(statusNow) === -1) { return }
var claimSysId = current.getUniqueValue() var validator = new x_2180676_claime_0.ClaimEaseValidator()
if (validator.hasAttachment(claimSysId)) { return }
gs.error( '[ClaimEase] Claim ' + current.getValue('number') + ' was inserted already submitted with no receipt attached. Returning it to draft so it cannot be approved.' )
// Cancel anything the approval flow already requested for this claim. var cancelled = 0 try { var approvals = new GlideRecord('sysapproval_approver') approvals.addQuery('source_table', 'x_2180676_claime_0_claim') approvals.addQuery('document_id', claimSysId) approvals.addQuery('state', 'IN', 'requested,not_requested') approvals.query() while (approvals.next()) { approvals.setValue('state', 'cancelled') if (approvals.update()) { cancelled++ } } } catch (e) { gs.error('[ClaimEase] Could not cancel approvals for a receiptless claim: ' + e) }
var claim = new GlideRecord('x_2180676_claime_0_claim') if (!claim.get(claimSysId)) { return } claim.setValue('approval_status', 'draft') claim.setValue('flow_started', false) claim.setValue('submitted_on', '')
// The approval decision fields must come back with the claim. Leaving // manager_approval at 'requested' on a draft is wrong on its own terms, and // it also stops the claim ever re-entering approval: the approval flow is // triggered by approval_status = submitted on create OR update, but its // first step does not re-ask an approver whose decision is already // 'requested'. A claim restored after its receipt arrives would therefore // look pending for ever with no approval task (observed on CLM0001089). claim.setValue('manager_approval', 'not_requested') claim.setValue('finance_approval', 'not_requested') claim.setValue( 'exception_reason', 'Returned to draft: no receipt or supporting document was attached when this claim was submitted.' )
// WHY setWorkflow(false) // This is the application correcting its own record, not a user acting on // it. "Protect Approval Fields" (order 150) allows manager_approval to be // written only by the recorded manager, a ClaimEase admin or the approval // automation, so an employee's own portal submission would be refused // here and the revert would fail outright - leaving a receiptless claim // approvable, which is the very thing this rule exists to prevent. // Suppressing the rule chain for this system write avoids fighting that // guard. It grants the user nothing: this path runs only inside this // rule, only for a claim submitted with no receipt, and it only ever // moves the claim backwards, away from approval. claim.setWorkflow(false) claim.update()
gs.info( '[ClaimEase] Claim ' + current.getValue('number') + ' returned to draft for a missing receipt (' + cancelled + ' pending approval(s) cancelled).' ) })(current, previous) ]]></script> <sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>claude.user</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2026-10-25 20:28:32</sys_created_on> <sys_domain>global</sys_domain> <sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path> <sys_id>00287ddfc308d3100d60f8ddd4013143</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>3</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>ClaimEase - Enforce Receipt On Submitted</sys_name> <sys_overrides/> <sys_package>global</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope>global</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>sys_script_00287ddfc308d3100d60f8ddd4013143</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>claude.user</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2026-11-01 16:07:28</sys_updated_on> <template/> <when>async_always</when> </sys_script></record_update>

<record_update table="sys_script"><sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <abort_action>false</abort_action> <access>package_private</access> <action_delete>false</action_delete> <action_insert>true</action_insert> <action_query>false</action_query> <action_update>false</action_update> <active>true</active> <add_message>false</add_message> <advanced>true</advanced> <change_fields>false</change_fields> <client_callable>false</client_callable> <collection>sys_attachment</collection> <condition/> <description>Returns a claim to submitted when its receipt arrives after the async receipt-enforcement rule had already sent it back to draft.</description> <execute_function>false</execute_function> <filter_condition table="sys_attachment">table_name=x_2180676_claime_0_claim^EQ<item goto="false" or="false" field="table_name" endquery="false" value="x_2180676_claime_0_claim" operator="=" newquery="false"/> <item goto="false" or="false" field="" endquery="true" value="" operator="=" newquery="false"/> </filter_condition> <is_rest>false</is_rest> <message/> <name>ClaimEase - Restore Claim On Receipt</name> <order>2000</order> <priority>100</priority> <rest_method/> <rest_method_text/> <rest_service/> <rest_service_text/> <rest_variables/> <role_conditions/> <script><![CDATA[/** * ClaimEase - Restore Claim On Receipt (sys_attachment, after insert, order 2000) * * PURPOSE * Closes the false-positive half of the receipt guarantee. * * "ClaimEase - Enforce Receipt On Submitted" (async, order 2000) returns a * claim to draft when it is submitted with no attachment. That is correct and * must stay immediate: a receiptless claim has to become un-approvable at * once, which is the point of the Defect 1 fix. It is also correct for the * Service Portal, where the widget copies the receipt onto the claim inside * the same request, so the async rule sees it. * * It is NOT correct when a claim is inserted as `submitted` and the receipt * is uploaded in a SECOND request moments later - how an integration, a * server script or a mobile client submits. The async rule fires in the gap, * finds nothing attached, and reverts a perfectly good claim. Reproduced on * CLM0001080: inserted 14:05:35, receipt available 14:05:37, claim still * returned to draft with its requested manager approval cancelled, and * nothing to put it back. * * When the receipt finally arrives, this rule returns the claim to * `submitted` so it re-enters approval. The existing before-update rules then * do their normal work: "Validate Claim" re-checks the receipt (now present), * "Lifecycle Stamps" re-stamps `submitted_on`, and "Start Approval Process" * re-arms the flow. * * HOW A REVERTED CLAIM IS RECOGNISED * NOT by the enforcement rule's `exception_reason` marker. The approval flow * writes its own exception text when it notices its approvals were cancelled, * and that write lands AFTER the marker, overwriting it (observed on * CLM0001089). The marker is therefore not durable. * * The structural evidence is durable. A claim the enforcement rule pulled * back is a draft with no `submitted_on`, `flow_started` false, and at least * one CANCELLED approval that the rule itself cancelled. A draft the employee * simply saved has never had an approval record at all, so it is left alone - * submitting it stays their decision. * * NO LOOP * The update re-fires the async enforcement rule, which now finds the * attachment and returns early. A later attachment finds the claim no longer * in draft and does nothing. * * HOW THE APPROVAL IS RE-ARMED * Nothing here asks for approval. The flow's trigger is already * `record_create_or_update` on the claim table with the condition * `approval_status=submitted` and strategy `unique_changes`, so simply * returning the claim to `submitted` re-triggers it. That works only because * the enforcement rule now resets `manager_approval` and `finance_approval` * to 'not_requested' when it pulls the claim back; the flow does not re-ask * an approver whose decision still reads 'requested'. Verified on CLM0001090, * which received a fresh `requested` approval for its manager one second * after its receipt arrived. */ ;(function executeRule(current, previous) { var CLAIM_TABLE = 'x_2180676_claime_0_claim'
if (('' + current.getValue('table_name')) !== CLAIM_TABLE) { return }
var claimSysId = '' + (current.getValue('table_sys_id') || '') if (!claimSysId) { return }
var claim = new GlideRecord(CLAIM_TABLE) if (!claim.get(claimSysId)) { return }
// Only a claim that was submitted and then pulled back, never a saved draft. if (('' + claim.getValue('approval_status')) !== 'draft') { return } if (('' + (claim.getValue('submitted_on') || '')) !== '') { return } if (claim.getValue('flow_started') == true || ('' + claim.getValue('flow_started')) === 'true') { return }
var cancelled = new GlideRecord('sysapproval_approver') cancelled.addQuery('source_table', CLAIM_TABLE) cancelled.addQuery('document_id', claimSysId) cancelled.addQuery('state', 'cancelled') cancelled.setLimit(1) cancelled.query() if (!cancelled.hasNext()) { return }
claim.setValue('approval_status', 'submitted') claim.setValue('exception_reason', '') claim.update()
gs.info( '[ClaimEase] Claim ' + claim.getValue('number') + ' was returned to submitted because its receipt arrived after the enforcement rule had run.' ) })(current, previous) ]]></script> <sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>claude.user</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2026-11-01 16:07:43</sys_created_on> <sys_domain>global</sys_domain> <sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path> <sys_id>ab8fbca9c35457500d60f8ddd401314a</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>ClaimEase - Restore Claim On Receipt</sys_name> <sys_overrides/> <sys_package>global</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope>global</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>sys_script_ab8fbca9c35457500d60f8ddd401314a</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>claude.user</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2026-11-01 16:07:43</sys_updated_on> <template/> <when>after</when> </sys_script></record_update>
